C.a: T1- The center has the best services. E2- It has reliable water, electricity, and police, while the edge doesn't. A3- In the U.S. rich people moved to the suburbs because they had cars and highways, but in Latin America the edge is where the poor live.
Living near the CBD is close to jobs, shops, and culture. In U.S. cities wealthy people moved out to the suburbs, but in Latin America the outskirts are squatter settlements with no services.

F.a: T1- The city is growing too fast to build pipes out to the edge. E2- Stimulus 2 shows Puerto Alba grew from 5.4 million to 9.6 million, and Stimulus 1 shows the periférico is on the outer edge, far from the CBD. A3- So many people there don't get clean water, and diseases spread.

Puerto Alba went from 5,400,000 to 9,600,000 people, and the squatter settlements are in the outermost ring of the city. The government can't build sewers and water lines fast enough to reach that far, so people lack sanitation.

Since it's a primate city that gained over 4 million people in 25 years, and the periferico is at the very edge away from downtown, buses don't reach it, so residents have really long commutes to jobs in the CBD.
